key_insight: WPNet shows that a graph neural network can heuristically infer geodesic representatives and word-equivalence structure in groups where the word problem is hard, enabling word reduction and length prediction without explicit algebraic rules.
engineering_relevance: This matters for post-quantum cryptography because it demonstrates that learned structural leakage can undermine group-based public-key schemes that rely on the apparent hardness of the word problem.
method: Represents unreduced group words as dynamic graph structures.
Trains a GNN to cluster algebraically equivalent elements in a continuous embedding space.
Adds a variant to predict geodesic length in Baumslag-Solitar and Artin groups.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful demonstrations on the Baumslag-Solitar group BS(1,2) and an Artin group, including an attack against the Wagner-Magyarik cryptosystem.
watch_item: The approach is heuristic rather than exact, so performance and security impact may depend strongly on the chosen group family, training data, and distribution shift.
paper_title: Learning the Word Problem: Geodesic Lengths and Cryptographic Applications
